sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 34 = check 33; Internal Quality Checks row 34 incl. column E annotation on combining verifiers in one flow)
.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r10/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (whole file; known false positive 'One criterion covering a whole flow', lines 59-64)
evidence: Static wording review of all 54 criterion descriptions (42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual, 2 constraints gate, 1 render gate). No criterion enumerates requirements and then waives most of them. Every binary description states its legs as 'must' steps and closes with one 'Fails if' list; functional/prompt.md:13 and polish/prompt.md:12 tell the judge 'A criterion is a conjunction: every step it lists must hold', so the body is the single full-credit bar. Multi-leg flows are the conjunctive bundling the skill lists as a known false positive (SKILL.md:64) and the internal workbook annotation endorses. Carve-outs found are narrow scope exclusions pointing at other criteria, not waivers of enumerated legs: functional/judge.toml:92 ('Running the draft is not part of this criterion'), :119 ('Undo behaviour is not judged here'), :254 (end reason scored elsewhere), :191 and :200 ('A change of quote style alone is not a failure'), :290 ('restored picture may be static'); polish/judge.toml:32 and :68 (Run output scored elsewhere), :59 ('saved' label not required). Explicit alternatives each resolve to one bar: functional/judge.toml:56 (triple click with or without line break), :155 (Redo disabled is enough, else click and replacements must not return), :371 (second-tab restore refused or added on top; the single bar is that revision five's source stays listed), :308 and :317 (void-attempt rule ends in a defined fail). functional/judge.toml:173 says 'One bar:' outright. gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 forbids a textarea/input showing the source and allows one used only to receive events: one consistent bar. Visual likert anchors 5..0 are monotonic and agree with visual/prompt.md:7. Counts stated inside descriptions match their own lists (polish/judge.toml:41 five actions, :50 three points, :68 five areas; functional/judge.toml:101 fifteen characters). Closest instance to the row's defect, examined and not failed: polish/judge.toml:23 lists nine control groups and then excludes controls that are disabled or absent. That is one conditional bar (every offered, enabled control reachable with visible focus, plus the unconditional editor-exit leg), and absent controls are graded by functional criteria, so it is not 'waive most'. Residual P3 wording drift, where the 'Fails if' list is narrower than the body (the conjunction rule resolves each, so not a defect): (a) polish/judge.toml:50 body requires Undo to become available after typing and Redo after Undo, while the fail list names only 'looks available when it has nothing to do'; (b) functional/judge.toml:281 and :299 body says the time-limit reason must appear 'within about ten seconds', the fail list says 'never ended'; (c) functional/judge.toml:155 Redo-restores-all-four leg, :74 Shift+Tab leg, :47 Shift+Arrow whole-selection leg and :236 valid-control leg are absent from their fail lists. Broken-app probe: an app whose Undo/Redo buttons are permanently disabled fails polish/judge.toml:50 on the body step 'Undo becomes available' under the conjunction rule. Conforming-alternative probe: an app whose triple click selects the line without its line break, or whose Redo is disabled after a new edit, is explicitly accepted. Limits: this is a wording review only; no configured judge run exists for these bytes (raw-evidence-index.json scope), so how the configured judge reads the narrower fail lists is not measured.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening, not required for this row: add the missing legs to the fail lists (polish/judge.toml:50 'or if Undo or Redo stays unavailable when it has something to do'; functional/judge.toml:281 and :299 'not ended within about ten seconds' instead of 'never ended').
